title: Japanese expansion: war in China to Pearl Harbor (1937–1941)
summary: How a clash near Beijing became full-scale war with China, and how Japan's push into South-East Asia led to US sanctions and the attack on Pearl Harbor.

keyterms.definition: 7 July 1937 clash between Japanese and Chinese troops near Beijing that escalated into the Second Sino-Japanese War.
Mass killing, rape and looting by Japanese troops after capturing the Chinese capital Nanjing in December 1937.
Alliance between the Chinese Nationalists (GMD) and Communists (CCP) against Japan, formed after the Xi'an Incident and formalised in 1937.
Prime Minister Konoe's 1938 declaration of a Japanese-led bloc of Japan, Manchukuo and China.
Japanese plan announced in 1940 for a self-sufficient Asian bloc under Japanese leadership, presented as liberation from Western colonialism.
1939 border war in which Soviet forces under Zhukov defeated the Japanese, discouraging a northern advance against the USSR.
September 1940 alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan, pledging mutual support if attacked by a power not yet at war, aimed at the USA.
US freezing of Japanese assets and halt to oil exports in summer 1941, after Japan occupied southern French Indochina.
US proposal of 26 November 1941 demanding Japanese withdrawal from China and Indochina; Tokyo treated it as an ultimatum.
Strategy of expanding into resource-rich South-East Asia (oil, rubber, tin) rather than north against the USSR.

questions.text: Full-scale war between Japan and China began after the ___ Incident in July 1937.
questions.explanation: A minor clash near Beijing on 7 July 1937 escalated because neither side was prepared to back down.

questions.prompt: Why did the Xi'an Incident of December 1936 matter for the war with Japan?
options: Chiang Kai-shek was forced towards a united front with the Communists against Japan
Japan agreed to withdraw from Manchuria
Mao Zedong was captured by the Nationalists
The USSR declared war on Japan
questions.explanation: Chiang was detained by his own commander Zhang Xueliang and pressed to stop fighting the CCP, leading to the Second United Front.

questions.statement: Japanese leaders expected a short war in China in 1937.
questions.explanation: Army planners expected China to collapse quickly. Instead the war became a costly stalemate that drained Japanese resources.

questions.prompt: What happened after Japanese forces captured Nanjing in December 1937?
options: A peaceful handover to a League commission
Mass atrocities against civilians and prisoners
Chiang Kai-shek surrendered
The USA declared war on Japan
questions.explanation: The Nanjing Massacre involved mass killing and rape over several weeks. Death toll estimates vary widely and remain politically contested.

questions.prompt: Put these events in chronological order.
items: Konoe announces a New Order in East Asia
questions.explanation: December 1936, July 1937, December 1937, November 1938.

questions.prompt: Where did Chiang Kai-shek's government relocate as Japan advanced?
options: Shanghai
Chongqing
Beijing
Guangzhou
questions.explanation: After losing Nanjing and then Wuhan (1938), the Nationalists moved their wartime capital up the Yangtze to Chongqing.

questions.prompt: Match each person to their role.

pairs.right: Japanese PM who proclaimed a New Order
Head of a Japanese-backed regime in Nanjing

questions.explanation: Wang Jingwei defected and led a collaborationist government from 1940.

questions.text: Soviet victory at ___ in 1939 discouraged Japan from expanding north.
questions.explanation: Defeat on the Mongolian border helped turn Japanese planners towards the southern advance.

questions.statement: The Panay incident of December 1937, when Japanese aircraft sank a US gunboat, led the USA to declare war.
questions.explanation: Japan apologised and paid compensation, and the isolationist USA accepted. It did, however, harden American opinion.

questions.prompt: What was the 'New Order in East Asia' (1938)?
options: A League plan to partition China
A Japanese-led bloc of Japan, Manchukuo and China
A US trade embargo
A Soviet–Chinese alliance
questions.explanation: Konoe's declaration showed Japan now aimed to dominate China politically and economically, not just win a border war.

lessons.title: The southern advance and Pearl Harbor

questions.prompt: Which event in Europe in 1940 created an opportunity for Japan in South-East Asia?
options: The defeat of France and the Netherlands by Germany
The Soviet invasion of Finland
Italy's invasion of Albania
The Spanish Civil War
questions.explanation: With France and the Netherlands defeated and Britain under pressure, their Asian colonies looked vulnerable.

questions.text: In September 1940 Japan signed the ___ Pact with Germany and Italy.
questions.explanation: The pact was designed to deter the USA by threatening a two-ocean war.

questions.prompt: Put these steps towards Pearl Harbor in order.
questions.explanation: September 1940, September 1940 (later in the month), April 1941, July 1941, 7 December 1941.

questions.prompt: What was the immediate US response to Japan's occupation of southern Indochina in July 1941?
options: Declaration of war
Freezing Japanese assets, which cut off oil supplies
Recognition of Manchukuo
Withdrawal of the Pacific Fleet to California
questions.explanation: The asset freeze, joined by Britain and the Dutch, stopped almost all Japanese oil imports, forcing a choice between retreat and war.

questions.statement: Japan imported most of its oil from the USA before 1941.
questions.explanation: This dependence made the embargo a crisis: Japan's navy estimated it had oil reserves for only about two years.

questions.prompt: Why did Japan sign a Neutrality Pact with the USSR in April 1941?
options: To protect its northern flank while it advanced south
To join the Allies against Germany
To return Manchuria to China
To gain Soviet oil
questions.explanation: The pact freed Japan to concentrate on the southern advance, and the USSR to focus on Europe.

questions.prompt: Match each US measure to what it did.

pairs.right: Allowed the USA to restrict trade from 1940
Response to Japan entering northern Indochina
Demanded withdrawal from China and Indochina

questions.explanation: US economic pressure escalated step by step from 1939 to 1941.

questions.text: General ___ became Japanese prime minister in October 1941.
questions.explanation: Konoe resigned after failing to reach agreement with the USA; Tojo's cabinet approved war if talks failed.

questions.prompt: What was the strategic aim of the attack on Pearl Harbor?
options: To invade Hawaii and then California
To cripple the US Pacific Fleet while Japan seized South-East Asia's resources
To force the USA to leave the League of Nations
To help Germany invade the USSR
questions.explanation: Japan hoped to buy time to build a defensive perimeter and negotiate from strength. US carriers were absent and escaped.

questions.statement: Japan presented the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere as freeing Asia from Western colonial rule.
questions.explanation: The slogan of liberation hid Japanese economic exploitation and harsh occupation policies.
